start: Phone signed in with Google on MettleUp, online

steps.action: Finish a workout and save it
user_sees: The finish screen as usual; no copy message
must_not: The copy running during the workout and slowing its saves

steps.action: Wait about 8 seconds, then open Settings, Backup and restore
user_sees: 'Your workouts are saved to your MettleUp account automatically. Last saved: <date>, <time>.'
must_not: The workout missing from the server copy
A copy of progress photos sent

steps.action: Edit the same workout's weight and wait
user_sees: 'Last saved' moves to the new time
must_not: The old version kept on the server
Two server items for one workout

start: Signed in, changes saved, app in use

steps.action: Press home to leave the app right after logging body weight
user_sees: Nothing on screen
must_not: The change waiting until the next app open when online

steps.action: Turn the internet off, add a routine, turn it back on
user_sees: Within a few seconds the waiting line clears in Settings
must_not: The routine never copied after the internet returns

start: Phone not signed in to MettleUp (or a build without the account)

steps.action: Save a workout
user_sees: The workout saved on the phone only
must_not: Any network call to the copy

steps.action: Open Settings, Backup and restore
user_sees: 'Keep your workouts on MettleUp'
'Sign in with Google to keep your workouts safe. MettleUp then saves your workouts, routines and body weight to your account by itself. On a new phone, sign in again and everything comes back.'
Button 'Continue with Google'
must_not: A 'Last saved' line for a phone that saves nothing

start: Signed in, no internet

steps.action: Save two changes offline, open Settings, Backup and restore
user_sees: '2 changes are waiting for the internet. They are saved by themselves when you are online.'
must_not: A change lost
A 'saved' line while nothing reached the server

start: Signed in, many workouts already copied

steps.action: Delete one workout
user_sees: The workout gone from History
must_not: The delete never reaching the server, so it comes back on a new phone

steps.action: Something wipes most of the history at once (more than 20 items and over half of the copy, or every workout)
user_sees: No delete sent; the server copy is brought back first on the next copy
must_not: The server copy emptied by one bad local state

start: Signed in member who belongs to a gym

steps.action: Save workouts, body weight and progress photos
user_sees: The privacy line 'Only you can see what is saved. Your gym cannot. Progress photos stay on this phone.'
must_not: The gym or its staff able to read member_items
Progress photo files sent to the server

start: App start on a phone signed in to MettleUp, online

steps.action: Root layout starts the copy watcher
user_sees: Nothing visible
must_not: Any listener or network call on a phone with no account

steps.action: 3 seconds later: scan the phone, queue what changed, send 100 at a time
user_sees: Settings 'Last saved' updates
must_not: A scan overlapping a workout save
A scan started by the copy's own writes (an endless loop)

start: Server refuses one damaged or too-big item in a batch

steps.action: Batch of 100 sent; server answers refused
user_sees: Nothing visible
must_not: The other 99 held back by one bad item

steps.action: Batch resent one by one; the refused item waits 6 hours
user_sees: The rest copied; the refused one stays in the queue
must_not: The refused item retried every few seconds

start: Server sign-in expired or the member's space is full

steps.action: Send a batch; server answers signed-out (or full)
user_sees: Settings line 'Sign in again to keep saving your workouts on MettleUp.' (or the full line)
must_not: The queue dropped
A 'Last saved' line that hides the problem

start: Another phone on the same account already saved a newer edit of an item

steps.action: Send this phone's older edit
user_sees: Server keeps its newer edit and names it
must_not: The newer edit overwritten

steps.action: Next copy
user_sees: The newer edit brought to this phone before anything else is sent
must_not: The older edit sent again and again

start: Phone holds the demo data and is signed in

steps.action: Scan runs
user_sees: Nothing queued
must_not: The sample member's made-up workouts sent to the server
